compliant_bourbon.png.note: Fully compliant distilled spirits label. Baseline.

warning_title_case.png.note: Heading in title case, not capitals. Jenny rejected one of these.

warning_body_bold.png.note: Entire warning bolded. §16.22(a)(2) forbids bolding the remainder.

warning_heading_not_bold.png.note: Heading in capitals but not bold.

abv_proof_only.png.note: Proof stated without percent by volume. §5.65 requires ABV.

small_bottle_50ml.png.note: Miniature. Selects the 1 mm type-size threshold under §16.22(b). No decidable defect, so PASS; the type-size caveat is advisory and reported separately.

imported_no_country.png.note: Imported product with no country of origin. §5.69.

photographed_off_angle.png.note: The same compliant label, rotated 7 degrees, unevenly lit, with specular glare across the upper third and JPEG noise — Jenny's 'photographed at weird angles, or the lighting is bad, or there's glare on the bottle'. Nothing about it is non-compliant, so the expected result is PASS: the test is whether a degraded capture still reads. Tesseract loses brand, class/type, ABV and net contents on this image and garbles the warning into 'rink ay beverages uring', which would fail a compliant label (EXT-09).

wine_commodity_gated.png.note: A wine label. Part 16 is universal so the warning checks run and must pass; the Part 5 distilled-spirits rules must report as unverified rather than failing, because hard-failing a wine label against a spirits citation is the confidently-wrong outcome (requirements §J-4).

warning_not_separated.png.note: Warning set as one more paragraph of body copy, same face and size as the marketing text around it; §16.21 requires it be separate and apart.
